allObjections.title: Migration cutover creates deployment freeze
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 blocks ALL products from using the new ≥95 bar until 100% of legacy ClearanceRecords are migrated. This creates a system-wide deployment freeze where no product can ship at the new standard until every legacy product is addressed, potentially blocking critical updates for weeks.

allObjections.title: Admin bottleneck for routine operations
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 requires admin role for ANY sub-95 deployment, even temporary staging deployments or emergency hotfixes. The 80-char rationale requirement and governance_record audit trail create friction that could delay critical fixes when the single admin is unavailable.

allObjections.title: Expiry cliff creates operational chaos
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 hard-expires overrides at 14 days OR next pipeline run, whichever is first. A product at 94 score suddenly fails Step 5 mid-deployment cycle with no warning, requiring emergency admin re-authorization even if nothing changed about the product's actual quality.

allObjections.title: No escape hatch for systemic scoring bugs
allObjections.detail: If the §7.6 scoring engine has a bug that artificially deflates scores across all products, the admin must issue individual expiring overrides for EVERY affected product every 14 days. There's no provision for a temporary system-wide scoring adjustment during bug fixes.

allObjections.title: Admin-only override risks abuse
allObjections.detail: The admin-only expiring override mechanism in §7.6.1 could be abused by admins to bypass the ≥95 GTM bar frequently, undermining the integrity of the standard. Without strict oversight or additional checks, this could lead to a culture of complacency where the override becomes the norm rather than the exception.

allObjections.title: Migration path complexity
allObjections.detail: The ClearanceRecord migration path outlined in §7.6.2 is complex and may introduce significant operational overhead. The requirement for re-evaluation and potential re-categorization of existing records could lead to delays and errors, especially if the migration script encounters unforeseen issues.

allObjections.title: Lack of operator involvement
allObjections.detail: By removing the operator-configurable knob and making the override admin-only, the proposal excludes operators from the decision-making process regarding GTM readiness. This could lead to frustration and disengagement from operators who feel they have valuable insights into product readiness.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback plan in case the new ≥95 canonical bar causes unintended consequences, such as a significant decrease in product deployments. This could lead to a situation where the system is worse than the status quo, as operators may struggle to meet the new bar.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not specify how the new admin-only expiring override mechanism will be tested to ensure it works correctly and does not introduce new bugs or security vulnerabilities. This lack of testing could lead to issues down the line, such as overrides not expiring correctly or being used in unintended ways.

allObjections.title: Potential for Abuse
allObjections.detail: The admin-only expiring override mechanism could be abused by admins to consistently deploy products with low scores, undermining the purpose of the ≥95 canonical bar. There is no clear mechanism in place to prevent or detect such abuse, which could lead to a degradation of the system's overall quality.

allObjections.title: Override Mechanism Complexity
allObjections.detail: The admin-only expiring override mechanism in §7.6.1 introduces significant complexity. The multiple rules for expiry and use, along with the need for detailed audit trails, could lead to implementation errors and increased maintenance burden.

allObjections.title: Migration Path Risk
allObjections.detail: The migration path for ClearanceRecord entities in §7.6.2 requires a complete inventory and re-evaluation of all existing entities. This process is time-consuming and risky, as any errors in re-evaluation could lead to incorrect status assignments and potential compliance issues.

allObjections.title: Conflation Invariant Redundancy
allObjections.detail: The mandatory invariant in §19.0 that states 'These are NEVER conflated in any operator-facing surface' is redundant with existing governance mechanisms in §10. This redundancy adds unnecessary complexity and could lead to confusion among operators.

allObjections.title: Migration Complexity
allObjections.detail: The migration path for ClearanceRecord entities is complex and may introduce errors or delays in the system.

allObjections.title: Admin Override Abuse
allObjections.detail: The admin-only expiring override mechanism could be abused by admins to bypass the ≥95 bar without proper justification.

allObjections.title: Near-GTM Band Elimination
allObjections.detail: Eliminating the Near-GTM 90–94 conditional band without a fallback clause may be too rigid and could lead to unnecessary delays in product deployment.

allObjections.title: Migration cutover deadlock risk
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 cutover gate requires 100% of pending ClearanceRecord entities to resolve to (a)/(b)/(c) before the ≥95 bar activates. But there is no mechanism preventing NEW ClearanceRecord entities from being created during the migration window — a product created mid-migration would be tagged `migration_pending` and could block cutover indefinitely if the engineering team cannot resolve all legacy entities. The cutover envelope `ca13v3_cutover_complete.v1` may never fire, leaving the system permanently on the old 75-bar standard.

allObjections.title: Override renewal loop — permanent sub-95 deployment
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 grants admin authority to issue a fresh override after expiry with no cooldown, no spending limit, and no escalation requirement. An admin can issue a 30-day override for a product at score 75, then immediately issue another 30-day override when the first expires, in perpetuity. The audit trail records each grant individually but nowhere does the spec cap the number of sequential overrides per product. This transforms the 'admin-only expiring override' into a de facto permanent escape hatch — the exact structural problem the CEO decision was meant to eliminate.

allObjections.title: Rationale quality gate is unenforceable
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 requires `rationale: string ≥ 80 chars; cannot match canonical stop-words set` but the stop-words list is not defined in the proposal, no validation logic is specified, and there is no human-review gate on rationale quality. An admin can write 'This is necessary for business reasons to proceed with deployment' (80+ chars, no obvious stop-words) and pass the envelope write. The spec provides no automated quality check and no escalation trigger for low-quality rationales, making the ≥80-char requirement a pure formality.

allObjections.title: Override floor rejection creates operational cliff
allObjections.detail: CA13A-v3-CT-3 specifies that `override_floor: 50` is REJECTED (not clamped). If an admin misconfigures the floor value and the override is rejected, the product falls immediately to the canonical ≥95 bar with no grace period. Unlike the migration path (which has a structured three-outcome resolution), there is no fallback mechanism for a rejected override envelope — the product simply fails Step 5 with no admin recourse documented in the spec. This creates a hard operational cliff where a single typo in an admin-issued override can halt deployment entirely.

allObjections.title: Migration outcome (c) creates legacy underclass incentive
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 outcome (c) allows admin annotation of ClearanceRecord as `legacy_pre_ca13v3` — these entities do not count toward any new §7.6 metrics. This creates a perverse incentive: any product that cannot score ≥95 can be re-categorized as legacy, removing it from the metric denominator entirely. The spec does not define who can apply outcome (c), what threshold triggers it, or whether there is a cap on legacy-archived entities. A product that scores 76 can be archived as legacy indefinitely, defeating the purpose of the ≥95 bar.

allObjections.title: Migration script failure risk
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 migration path lacks rollback mechanisms for failed re-evaluations. If the migration script encounters corrupted ClearanceRecord data during inventory pass, it could cascade failures across multiple products without recovery options. The conformance test CA13A-v3-CT-6 doesn't cover partial-failure states.

allObjections.title: Override expiry race condition
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 expiry rule 1 (next pipeline run) creates deployment race conditions. If two pipeline runs trigger simultaneously for the same product, override expiration timing becomes unpredictable. Audit envelope emission lacks atomicity guarantees with pipeline execution states.

allObjections.title: Guard() cross-reference gap
allObjections.detail: B-Q1 EXECUTOR_REGISTRY cross-reference doesn't resolve Slot 10 #34's concern about BaseAgent.guard() argument validation. The spec doesn't mandate how authorityNeeded sets are populated for Agent #26's dual-authority requirement per CA-9-Q4(b).

allObjections.title: Legacy categorization loophole
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 outcome (c) lets admins bypass migration via legacy_archived status without score verification. This creates an audit trail gap where pre-CA13v3 products avoid scrutiny indefinitely under the new standard.

allObjections.title: Override loophole persists
allObjections.detail: In §7.6.1 the proposal replaces the operator-config knob with an admin-only expiring override, but it still preserves a discretionary sub-95 escape hatch. Because admins can re-issue overrides repeatedly, the effective threshold can remain below 95 indefinitely, just with more ceremony and audit logging.

allObjections.title: Migration cutover is under-specified
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 says the ≥95 bar takes effect only after 100% of legacy ClearanceRecords resolve, but it does not specify a bounded enforcement path for stuck or abandoned records. A single unresolved or disputed legacy row could block cutover forever, or force ad hoc legacy-archiving decisions that weaken the standard.

allObjections.title: Dual-bar UI confusion risk
allObjections.detail: §19.0 adds a mandatory anti-conflation invariant and surface-labeling, yet the artifact still allows both the Self-Audit 95/95 threshold and the GTM bar to coexist in operator-facing surfaces. Without a single authoritative display contract, operators may misread one score as satisfying the other, especially during migration when old and new ClearanceRecords coexist.

allObjections.title: Migration cutover stalls entire bar
allObjections.detail: §7.6.2 requires 100% ClearanceRecord resolution (a/b/c outcomes) before emitting ca13v3_cutover_complete.v1 and activating the ≥95 bar. No timeout, partial-cutover path, or fallback for products lacking recent pipeline runs is defined, so a single stuck legacy record freezes the canonical threshold indefinitely.

allObjections.title: Expiring override window too wide
allObjections.detail: §7.6.1 allows admin to set expires_at up to granted_at+30 days and ties one expiry trigger to 'next pipeline run,' which may be weeks away. This creates a controllable multi-week sub-95 deployment window with only governance_record_entry audit, weaker than the v2 operator knob it replaces.

allObjections.title: Conformance tests lack enforcement spec
allObjections.detail: CA13A-v3-CT-1 through CT-8 define role checks and rejection envelopes, yet §15.1 and BaseAgent.guard() cross-references in CA-13-B-v3-Q1 never map these new gtm_bar_admin_override.v1 kinds into the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY or ScoreEvaluator.js decision matrix.

adversarial.precedent: The 2017 Equifax data breach (CVE-2017-5638) resulted from a known vulnerability with a patch available but not applied. The underlying governance failure was a systematic override mechanism where the risk of 'not patching' was perceived as lower than the operational cost of patching — creating a permanent escape hatch that persisted until catastrophe. CA-13 v3's admin-only expiring override with no spending limit replicates the same structural failure: a governance mechanism that is individually compliant but collectively catastrophic when used repeatedly on the same asset.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: CA-13 v3 attempts to resolve a Panel impasse via CEO Locked-Rule-13 fiat, but the resulting mechanism still conflates two semantically distinct concepts — Self-Audit 95/95 (a governance quality gate measuring internal process integrity) and GTM Readiness ≥95 (a launch readiness gate measuring product market-readiness) — by forcing them to the same numeric threshold. The proposal provides no empirical basis for why these two orthogonal dimensions should share a single number, and the §19.0 invariant ('These are NEVER conflated in any operator-facing surface') directly contradicts the structural decision to set them to the same value. Deferring until the Panel can establish an independent empirical basis for the GTM bar — rather than anchoring it to the governance threshold by administrative decree — would produce a more defensible and durable standard.

CA-13-A-v3-Q1.pick_text: Strengthen — expiry default 7 days (not 14), hard bounds [1,14]; rationale-quality validation requires ≥120 chars (not 80).
CA-13-A-v3-Q1.rationale: The 14-day default is too permissive given the absence of any override-spending limit or cooldown mechanism identified in the adversarial pass. Shortening to 7 days default and tightening the rationale quality gate to 120 chars reduces the surface area for override abuse without fundamentally altering the mechanism's structure.

CA-13-A-v3-Q2.pick_text: Strengthen toward audit — every §11 Step 5 evaluation consulting an override emits additional `step5_override_consulted.v1` envelope alongside `gtm_bar_admin_override_used.v1`.
CA-13-A-v3-Q2.rationale: The dual-envelope approach strengthens auditability without altering the override mechanism itself. The additional envelope provides a clearer signal for automated monitoring dashboards and reduces the forensic effort required to detect override renewal loops.

CA-13-A-v3-Q3.pick_text: Ratify but with redundancy fix — keep the invariant but DELETE §19.0 paragraph table (invariant alone suffices; §10 governance-mechanisms table already covers it).
CA-13-A-v3-Q3.rationale: The mandatory invariant is the binding element; the §19.0 paragraph table is descriptive and redundant with §10's governance-mechanisms table. Removing the paragraph eliminates the redundancy concern raised at v2 re-Panel while preserving the enforceable invariant.

CA-13-B-v3-Q1.pick_text: Reject — wording remains too vague without actual §15.5 sibling row-table populate; defer entire CA-13-B until that engineering dispatch ships.
CA-13-B-v3-Q1.rationale: The cross-reference to EXECUTOR_REGISTRY and BaseAgent.guard() is a citation, not a specification. Without the actual sibling row-table populate in §15.5, CA-13-B v3 ratification would lock in approval of language that references non-existent implementation details. Deferral until the engineering dispatch ships is the appropriate path.

CA-13-B-v3-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with `membership` rename — Agent #26 sibling becomes `orchestra-membership-executor`; Agent #21 stays `crawl-write-executor`.
CA-13-B-v3-Q2.rationale: Slot 2's objection is well-founded: 'admission' is narrower than the ongoing membership-management duties Agent #26 owns per §8.1. The rename to 'orchestra-membership-executor' better reflects the agent's charter and is a low-cost improvement that resolves a legitimate naming precision concern.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The override renewal loop objection (objection 2) is the most structurally dangerous: it transforms a time-bounded exception into a permanent escape hatch without any spending limit or cooldown. Any ratification of the v3 spine should include a mandatory review of whether override-spending limits are within scope for CA-13 or require a separate follow-on amendment.

objections.title: Migration script failure risk
objections.detail: §7.6.2 migration path lacks rollback mechanisms for failed re-evaluations. If the migration script encounters corrupted ClearanceRecord data during inventory pass, it could cascade failures across multiple products without recovery options. The conformance test CA13A-v3-CT-6 doesn't cover partial-failure states.

objections.title: Override expiry race condition
objections.detail: §7.6.1 expiry rule 1 (next pipeline run) creates deployment race conditions. If two pipeline runs trigger simultaneously for the same product, override expiration timing becomes unpredictable. Audit envelope emission lacks atomicity guarantees with pipeline execution states.

objections.title: Guard() cross-reference gap
objections.detail: B-Q1 EXECUTOR_REGISTRY cross-reference doesn't resolve Slot 10 #34's concern about BaseAgent.guard() argument validation. The spec doesn't mandate how authorityNeeded sets are populated for Agent #26's dual-authority requirement per CA-9-Q4(b).

objections.title: Legacy categorization loophole
objections.detail: §7.6.2 outcome (c) lets admins bypass migration via legacy_archived status without score verification. This creates an audit trail gap where pre-CA13v3 products avoid scrutiny indefinitely under the new standard.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: During migration, if a product scores 80 under the new bar (failing) but had 78 under the old bar (passing), and the admin is unavailable to issue override, it becomes blocked while previously deployable. Simultaneous override expiry and pipeline run could cause production outages for borderline-scoring critical systems.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The migration prerequisite creates systemic deployment freeze risk for all pre-existing products, while the admin-only override concentrates critical path dependencies on limited personnel. Given unresolved edge cases in override expiry timing and legacy recategorization loopholes, deferring until atomic migration transitions and override-use idempotency are proven would reduce operational hazard.

CA-13-A-v3-Q1.pick_text: Strengthen — expiry default 7 days (not 14), hard bounds [1,14]; rationale-quality validation requires ≥120 chars (not 80).
CA-13-A-v3-Q1.rationale: Shorter default expiry reduces override exposure window; extended rationale requirement addresses Slot 9 #29 audit-quality concerns without requiring full redesign.

CA-13-A-v3-Q2.pick_text: Strengthen — append "Any future Panel proposal to re-introduce sub-95 conditional path is a candidate for CEO-Locked-Rule-13 dispositional veto by default, given the admin-only expiring override per §7.6.1."
CA-13-A-v3-Q2.rationale: Preempts regression attempts while preserving Panel authority, addressing Slot 10 #33's loophole concern more definitively than silent removal.

CA-13-A-v3-Q3.pick_text: Ratify but with redundancy fix — keep the invariant but DELETE §19.0 paragraph table (invariant alone suffices; §10 governance-mechanisms table already covers it).
CA-13-A-v3-Q3.rationale: Resolves Slot 6 #19's redundancy objection while retaining the core anti-conflation enforcement.

CA-13-B-v3-Q1.pick_text: Strengthen — also inline schema snippet of BaseAgent.guard() arguments directly in §15-intro text, not just cross-reference.
CA-13-B-v3-Q1.rationale: Directly addresses Slot 10 #34's specificity gap by showing authorityNeeded set structure, preventing implementation drift.

CA-13-B-v3-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with `membership` rename — Agent #26 sibling becomes `orchestra-membership-executor`; Agent #21 stays `crawl-write-executor`.
CA-13-B-v3-Q2.rationale: "Membership" better reflects Agent #26's ongoing duties per §8.1 (Slot 2 #20) while preserving capability-keyed clarity.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Migration script must include circuit-breaker to pause on >5% failure rate during inventory pass.

objections.title: Override loophole persists
objections.detail: In §7.6.1 the proposal replaces the operator-config knob with an admin-only expiring override, but it still preserves a discretionary sub-95 escape hatch. Because admins can re-issue overrides repeatedly, the effective threshold can remain below 95 indefinitely, just with more ceremony and audit logging.

objections.title: Migration cutover is under-specified
objections.detail: §7.6.2 says the ≥95 bar takes effect only after 100% of legacy ClearanceRecords resolve, but it does not specify a bounded enforcement path for stuck or abandoned records. A single unresolved or disputed legacy row could block cutover forever, or force ad hoc legacy-archiving decisions that weaken the standard.

objections.title: Dual-bar UI confusion risk
objections.detail: §19.0 adds a mandatory anti-conflation invariant and surface-labeling, yet the artifact still allows both the Self-Audit 95/95 threshold and the GTM bar to coexist in operator-facing surfaces. Without a single authoritative display contract, operators may misread one score as satisfying the other, especially during migration when old and new ClearanceRecords coexist.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If an admin is pressured to keep shipping products under 95, the new design can institutionalize repeated temporary overrides rather than forcing a hard stop. That is worse than the current status quo if the current system at least makes sub-95 releases visibly exceptional, because the proposal normalizes them through a formal workflow and audit trail.
adversarial.precedent: The Kubernetes admission-control and feature-gate ecosystems have shown that temporary escape hatches often become long-lived operational dependencies when expiry and re-approval are easy to renew. Similar drift has also been seen with emergency change windows in large enterprises, where 'temporary' exceptions became the default path.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this proposal is that it adds governance complexity without actually eliminating the core risk: a sub-95 release path. The admin-only override, migration prerequisite, and dual-bar UI rules introduce more state transitions, more audit surfaces, and more failure modes, while still leaving room for recurring exceptions and ambiguous operator interpretation. If the goal is a clean safety boundary, deferral until the override lifecycle and migration cutover are mechanically airtight would be prudent.

CA-13-A-v3-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q1.rationale: None of the listed choices fully resolves the permanent-loophole problem introduced by repeated admin overrides, and the migration prerequisite is too open-ended. The proposal still allows practical sub-95 shipping through renewals, so ratifying as drafted would be premature.

CA-13-A-v3-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q2.rationale: Eliminating the Near-GTM band is directionally sound, but the options do not address the operational ambiguity of the remaining override path. Without tighter constraints on override renewal and cutover, the safety valve remains effectively equivalent to a second conditional path.

CA-13-A-v3-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q3.rationale: The invariant helps, but the proposal does not give a sufficiently crisp UI enforcement model to prevent conflation in practice. The listed options either add more policy without solving surface ambiguity or remove too much useful context.

CA-13-B-v3-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-v3-Q1.rationale: The cross-reference-only approach is too vague for an executor/guard mechanism that appears safety-critical. Bundling the row-table populate would still leave unresolved whether the runtime enforcement spec is complete and testable, so defer until the implementation dispatch lands.

CA-13-B-v3-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-v3-Q2.rationale: The naming options all trade off traceability, clarity, and role semantics, but none convincingly matches the underlying authority model described in the canonical reference. The proposal needs a stricter naming contract tied to agent IDs and permissions before ratification.

perReviewer.overallNotes: Net: the spine is closer to a policy patch than a robust safety boundary. My vote remains reject/defer until override renewal, migration cutover, and display semantics are all mechanically closed.

objections.title: Migration cutover stalls entire bar
objections.detail: §7.6.2 requires 100% ClearanceRecord resolution (a/b/c outcomes) before emitting ca13v3_cutover_complete.v1 and activating the ≥95 bar. No timeout, partial-cutover path, or fallback for products lacking recent pipeline runs is defined, so a single stuck legacy record freezes the canonical threshold indefinitely.

objections.title: Expiring override window too wide
objections.detail: §7.6.1 allows admin to set expires_at up to granted_at+30 days and ties one expiry trigger to 'next pipeline run,' which may be weeks away. This creates a controllable multi-week sub-95 deployment window with only governance_record_entry audit, weaker than the v2 operator knob it replaces.

objections.title: Conformance tests lack enforcement spec
objections.detail: CA13A-v3-CT-1 through CT-8 define role checks and rejection envelopes, yet §15.1 and BaseAgent.guard() cross-references in CA-13-B-v3-Q1 never map these new gtm_bar_admin_override.v1 kinds into the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY or ScoreEvaluator.js decision matrix.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the migration script encounters more than a handful of pre-v3 ClearanceRecords without fresh scores, the cutover gate never fires; the system remains permanently on the old 75-bar for all products, eliminating even the partial pressure toward 95 that existed under the v2 operator-configurable knob.
adversarial.precedent: Facebook's 2010s 'temporary' feature-flag exceptions for high-priority launches that accumulated into permanent low-quality paths because migration and expiry logic were never enforced at cutover time.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The v3 spine still embeds a permanent admin-only escape hatch whose 30-day bound and pipeline-run trigger are too loose to be a genuine safety invariant. Combined with the all-or-nothing migration prerequisite, it risks locking the platform at the pre-CA-13 quality floor for an indeterminate period while adding new audit surface that itself requires governance. Deferral until a fully specified enforcement layer and bounded migration window are engineered is the safer course.

CA-13-A-v3-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q1.rationale: All options retain either the wide 30-day window or the migration cutover gate that can stall the bar change.

CA-13-A-v3-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q2.rationale: No option closes the audit-gap between override grant and actual Step 5 use.

CA-13-A-v3-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v3-Q3.rationale: Invariant language alone does not address the missing UI-enforcement mapping to ScoreEvaluator.js.

CA-13-B-v3-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-v3-Q1.rationale: Cross-reference without concrete EXECUTOR_REGISTRY entries leaves the new override kinds unenforced.

CA-13-B-v3-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-v3-Q2.rationale: Capability naming remains underspecified relative to the dual-authority guard required by Agent #26.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All five questions share the same structural weakness: new governance envelopes are declared without corresponding executor-registry wiring or migration-timeout logic.
